claim: YouTube's own platform disclosure states its Partner Program (the gate to ad, subscription, and Super Chat monetization) passed 2 million members as of August 2021, with new-channel enrollment in 2020 more than doubling versus 2019.
stance_target: Establishing a platform-disclosed count of actually-monetizing YouTube creators, distinct from the raw count of channels that clear the subscriber eligibility threshold
scope_conditions: Company statement by Neal Mohan (YouTube Chief Product Officer) in an official blog post, reported by The Verge, August 23, 2021; a raw membership count, not validated by independent audit, and YouTube did not disclose how many of the 2 million actually earn any revenue in a given period
quoted_support: YouTube's Partner Program, which allows users to make money off their videos, has passed the 2 million creator mark, the company said Monday... Neal Mohan, chief product officer at YouTube, said in a blog post that the number of new channels joining the program in 2020 more than doubled when compared to 2019
numbers: >100% YoY growth in new enrollments, 2019 to 2020
channels making six figures up 35% YoY (no absolute count given)

claim: Cross-referencing YouTube's own 2 million YPP-member disclosure (Aug 2021) against Rieder et al.'s independently-crawled census of 4,415,180 channels with 1,000+ subscribers (the YPP eligibility floor, crawled 2019-2020) implies only about 45% of subscriber-eligible channels actually enroll in monetization, roughly doubling the true attempt rate compared to using the raw subscriber-tier channel count as a denominator.
stance_target: Raw channel counts above the 1,000-subscriber eligibility threshold are an accurate denominator for 'creators who attempted to earn income from YouTube'
scope_conditions: Cross-source computation: YouTube's self-reported 2 million YPP members (Aug 2021) is a single point-in-time platform disclosure with no published audit trail; Rieder et al.'s 4,415,180-channel count is from an independent academic crawl one to two years earlier (2019-2020), so the two figures are not perfectly time-matched, and YPP membership was still growing rapidly (>100% YoY in 2020) which could narrow or widen the gap depending on exact timing
quoted_support: YouTube's Partner Program... has passed the 2 million creator mark [Aug 2021]. (Cross-referenced with Rieder et al. 2020's independent count of 4,415,180 channels with 1,000+ subscribers.)
numbers: ~2.2x denominator inflation if raw subscriber count is used instead of actual YPP membership
time_period: channels crawled 2019-2020; YPP membership disclosed August 2021
